title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's Warning to the Nation: Political Democracy vs Social Democracy (1949)
summary: On November 25, 1949, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar delivered his monumental final address to the Constituent Assembly, warning that political democracy cannot survive without social and economic democracy.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 157: அம்பேத்கரும் எச்.பி. சக்சேனாவும்: “என்னைப் பெயரிடாதீர்கள்; சீக்கிரமே இறந்துவிடுவேன்”
full_text:
On November 25, 1949, the Constituent Assembly in New Delhi gathered for the final reading of the Constitution of India.

Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee, rose to deliver his concluding address. Colleagues had spent days showering praise upon his legal brilliance, but Ambedkar turned his gaze toward the profound perils facing the young republic:

"On the 26th of January 1950, we are going to enter into a life of contradictions.
In politics we will have equality, and in social and economic life we will have inequality. In politics we will be recognizing the principle of one man one vote and one vote one value. But in our social and economic structure, by reason of our caste system and economic disparities, we continue to deny the principle of one man one value!

How long shall we continue to live this life of contradictions? How long shall we continue to deny equality in our social and economic life?
If we continue to deny it for long, we will do so only by putting our political democracy in peril. We must remove this contradiction at the earliest possible moment, or else those who suffer from inequality will blow up the structure of political democracy which this Assembly has so laboriously built up!"

The chamber was gripped by the solemn power of Ambedkar’s foresight. He established that political liberty without social and economic justice is a house built upon shifting sand.

moral: Political freedom is fragile without social and economic equality; true democracy must recognize the equal worth of every human being.
